purpose: Retrieval index for the generation skill. Two to three of these are meant to be selected per request as exemplars, matched on category, technique, and route. Regenerate after every conversion wave.

charts.title: Bar Chart
charts.data_shape: { letter: string; frequency: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Compares a single value across a small set of named categories, sorted so the ranking reads off the length.

charts.title: Line Chart
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; value: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: A single continuous quantity tracked over time when the shape of the trend matters more than individual readings.

charts.title: Area Chart
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; value: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: One time series where accumulated volume or magnitude should feel weighty, not just the trend line itself.

charts.title: Pie Chart
charts.data_shape: { name: string; value: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Part of a whole across a handful of categories when the shares, not the precise values, are the point.

charts.title: Multi-Line Chart
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; division: string; rate: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Several time series on one shared axis when you need to compare their shapes and pick one out by hovering.
keywords: one row per series per date

charts.title: Stacked Area Chart
charts.data_shape: { industries: readonly Industry[]; rows: UnemploymentRow[] }
charts.when_to_use: Composition of a total over time when both the running total and each part's contribution matter.
keywords: part of a whole over time

charts.title: Scatterplot with Shapes
charts.data_shape: { points: { species: string; sepalLength: number; sepalWidth: number }[]; species: string[]; }
charts.when_to_use: Correlation between two measures across a few groups when color alone must not carry the grouping, as in print or for colorblind readers.
keywords: two numeric columns plus a label

charts.title: Band Chart
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; low: number; high: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: A range per date, a min and max or a confidence interval, rather than one value per date.

charts.title: Difference Chart
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; sanFrancisco: number; newYork: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Two series measured on the same dates when the gap between them, and which one is ahead, is the story.

charts.title: Normalized Stacked Area
charts.data_shape: { rows: GenerationRow[]; sources: readonly Source[] }
charts.when_to_use: Share of a total over time when relative composition matters and the absolute total should be suppressed.
keywords: part of a whole over time

charts.title: Area Chart with Missing Data
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; close: number | null }[]
charts.when_to_use: A filled time series with holes in it, drawn so the gaps read as absent data instead of being bridged.

charts.title: Line Chart with Missing Data
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; close: number | null }[]
charts.when_to_use: Same as an ordinary line chart but the series has holes, and the breaks should be visible rather than interpolated across.

charts.title: Index Chart
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; symbol: string; close: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Several series at wildly different absolute levels compared by relative growth from a starting date the reader can move.

charts.title: Connected Scatterplot
charts.data_shape: { year: number; miles: number; gas: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Two measures plotted against each other with time as the path through the plot, when the trajectory doubles back on itself.
keywords: one row per year with two measures

charts.title: Change Line Chart
charts.data_shape: { closes: { date: Date; close: number }[]; basis: number }
charts.when_to_use: One series expressed as percent change from a fixed basis, with gains and losses shaded on either side of parity.
keywords: date and value plus a reference value

charts.title: Revenue by Music Format
charts.data_shape: { rows: FormatYear[]; formats: readonly MusicFormat[] }
charts.when_to_use: Successive categories displacing one another across years, labeled in place on their own bands instead of through a legend.
keywords: part of a whole over time
one row per year with a column per category

charts.title: Diverging Bar Chart
charts.data_shape: { state: string; pop2010: number; pop2019: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Ranked signed values where growth and decline should read as opposite directions from a zero baseline.
keywords: two values per row to difference

charts.title: Slope Chart
charts.data_shape: { rows: { country: string; before: number; after: number }[]; columns: [string, string]; }
charts.when_to_use: Exactly two time points across many named items, so each item's rise or fall reads as the direction of its own line.
keywords: one row per item with two values

charts.title: Marimekko Chart
charts.data_shape: { name: string; value?: number; children?: Data[] }
charts.when_to_use: Two categorical dimensions at once, where column width carries one total and the stacked height carries the split inside it.

charts.title: Inequality in Cities
charts.data_shape: { city: string; start: number; end: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: A start and end value per row drawn as an arrow, ranked by the size of the move rather than by either endpoint.
keywords: one row per place with two values

charts.title: Survival Rates
charts.data_shape: { steps: string[]; conditions: { name: string; values: number[] }[]; }
charts.when_to_use: Several series across a few ordered stages where every value is labeled in place, extending a two-column slope chart to four.
keywords: one row per group with a value per stage

charts.title: Diverging Stacked Bar Chart
charts.data_shape: { question: string; 'Strongly disagree': number; Disagree: number; Neutral: number; Agree: number; 'Strongly agree': number; }[]
charts.when_to_use: Likert-style agreement scales, where the neutral midpoint sits at zero and disagreement extends to the left.
keywords: part of a whole with a midpoint
one row per question with a count per option

charts.title: Stacked Horizontal Bar Chart
charts.data_shape: { ageGroups: string[]; rows: { state: string; values: number[] }[]; }
charts.when_to_use: Long row labels with an internal breakdown, when the absolute row totals still need to be comparable.
keywords: part of a whole by row
one row per label with a value per subgroup

charts.title: Stacked Normalized Horizontal Bar

keywords: part of a whole by row
one row per label with a value per subgroup

charts.title: Methods of Comparison
charts.data_shape: { id: string; name: string; a: number; b: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Choosing how to encode change between two values, shown as six small maps of difference, relative change and log ratio side by side.
keywords: one row per region with two values

charts.title: Bollinger Bands
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; close: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: A price series wrapped in a rolling mean and a volatility envelope computed from a moving standard deviation.

charts.title: Calendar View
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; value: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Daily values across several years laid out as a weeks-by-weekday grid, so weekday and seasonal patterns surface.

charts.title: Moving Average
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; count: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: A noisy daily count where the choice of smoothing window is itself the subject, with several windows drawn over the raw series.

charts.title: Global Temperature Trends
charts.data_shape: { anomalies: { date: Date; value: number }[]; trend: { date: Date; value: number }[]; }
charts.when_to_use: Many noisy dated readings with a smoothed trend over them, points colored by their sign around a zero reference.
keywords: raw readings plus a smoothed series

charts.title: Sea Ice Extent
charts.data_shape: { year: number; values: { date: Date; value: number }[] }[]
charts.when_to_use: Many years of one seasonal cycle overlaid on a single day-of-year axis, colored by year so decade-scale drift shows.
keywords: one series per year of dated values
annual repeats of the same measure

charts.title: Marey's Trains
charts.data_shape: { stations: Station[]; trains: { id: string; number: number; type: ServiceType; direction: 'N' | 'S'; stops: Stop[]; }[]; }
charts.when_to_use: Vehicles moving along a fixed route, with time across and distance along the route down, so each line's slope is its speed.

charts.title: US Population by State
charts.data_shape: { rows: { year: number; byState: Record<string, number> }[]; years: number[]; states: string[]; regions: readonly string[]; regionByState: Map<string, string>; }
charts.when_to_use: Shows how a total grew while its many constituent parts shifted share, with the biggest bands named in place rather than in a legend.

charts.title: Line Chart with Tooltip
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; close: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: A single time series where the reader needs the exact value at any date, not just the shape.

charts.title: Realtime Horizon Chart

charts.title: World History Timeline
charts.data_shape: { civilizations: { civilization: string; start: number; end: number; region: string }[]; regions: string[]; }
charts.when_to_use: Many overlapping intervals with start and end dates, packed into as few rows as their spans allow.

charts.title: Predator and Prey
charts.when_to_use: An animated simulation where two coupled quantities cycle, shown as time series beside the phase orbit they trace.

charts.title: New Zealand Tourists 1921-2018
charts.data_shape: { points: { date: Date; value: number }[]; events: { date: Date; label: string }[]; }
charts.when_to_use: A long series spanning orders of magnitude, where a linear/log toggle and dated event rules explain the turns.

charts.title: Normal Quantile Plot
charts.data_shape: number[]
charts.when_to_use: Tests whether one sample is normally distributed, by plotting it against the normal scores it would have if it were.

charts.title: Hexbin
charts.data_shape: { carat: number; price: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: A scatterplot so dense that points overplot; hexagonal bins encode count as color instead.

charts.title: Hexbin Area
charts.data_shape: { carat: number; price: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Same dense-scatter binning as its color-encoded sibling, but count is encoded as mark size, which reads on any background.

charts.title: Volcano Contours
charts.data_shape: { values: number[]; columns: number; rows: number }
charts.when_to_use: A regular grid of measurements where the contour bands themselves are the subject, like elevation or a survey.

charts.title: Vector Field
charts.when_to_use: A field with direction and magnitude at every point, where arrows read better than color alone.

charts.title: Voronoi Stippling
charts.when_to_use: Renders a continuous density field as discrete dots, so tone comes from dot spacing rather than fill.

charts.title: Mirrored Beeswarm
charts.data_shape: { name: string; weight: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Shows every individual observation's position along one axis without overlap, spread symmetrically about a center line.

charts.title: Voronoi Labels
charts.data_shape: { x: number; y: number; label: string }[]
charts.when_to_use: Labels a scattered set of named points by giving each the room its Voronoi cell allows, dropping the cramped ones.

charts.title: Kernel Density Estimation
charts.data_shape: number[]
charts.when_to_use: Shows a distribution's shape without the arbitrary bin edges of a histogram, and how much the bandwidth choice matters.

charts.title: Q-Q Plot
charts.data_shape: { a: number[]; b: number[] }
charts.when_to_use: Compares two samples' whole distributions against each other, not just their means, on a square 45-degree frame.

charts.title: Contours
charts.when_to_use: Contours a function evaluated on a grid, with log-spaced thresholds because the values span orders of magnitude.

charts.title: Density Contours
charts.data_shape: { waiting: number; eruptions: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Reveals clusters in a scatterplot by estimating 2D density, better than hexbins when the shape of the modes matters.

charts.title: Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram
charts.data_shape: { id: number; bv: number; magnitude: number; color: string }[]
charts.when_to_use: A dense scatterplot on a deliberately inverted axis, where the population's clusters get named annotations.

charts.title: PSR B1919+21
charts.data_shape: number[][]
charts.when_to_use: Many sequential traces stacked with heavy overlap, so each row's peaks rise over the rows behind it.

charts.title: Impact of Vaccines
charts.data_shape: { regions: string[]; years: number[]; incidence: (number | null)[][]; startYear: number; endYear: number; eventYear: number; }
charts.when_to_use: A category-by-year matrix where a single intervention date should visibly split the grid before and after.

charts.title: Electric Usage
charts.data_shape: { usage: number[]; days: number; hoursPerDay: number; yearStart: Date; }
charts.when_to_use: A full year of hourly readings as a day-by-hour grid, with a diverging ramp so sign reads as clearly as magnitude.

charts.title: Population by Age
charts.data_shape: { cells: { year: number; age: number; value: number }[]; firstYear: number; lastYear: number; maxAge: number; }
charts.when_to_use: A year-by-age grid where cohorts read as diagonals, so historic events leave visible streaks across generations.

charts.title: Variable Color Line
charts.data_shape: { observations: { date: Date; temperature: number; condition: string }[]; conditions: { key: string; label: string; color: string }[]; }
charts.when_to_use: One continuous series whose segments must be colored by a categorical attribute that changes along the line.

charts.title: Gradient Encoding
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; temperature: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: One series where the value should be legible from color as well as height, using a continuous ramp along the stroke.

charts.title: Threshold Encoding
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; temperature: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: One series that should read as above or below a single cutoff, with the line's color flipping hard at that line.

charts.title: Styled Axes
charts.data_shape: { date: Date; value: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Compares axis treatments side by side on one series, to decide how much axis a chart actually needs.

charts.title: Color Legend
charts.when_to_use: Builds the legend itself rather than a chart, covering continuous, diverging, threshold and discrete scales.

charts.title: Color Schemes
charts.when_to_use: A reference sheet of the built-in color ramps and palettes, for picking one before building a chart.

charts.title: Watercolor
charts.when_to_use: An illustrative map where hand-drawn wobble and a four-coloring matter more than precise borders or data values.

charts.title: Inline Labels
charts.data_shape: { points: { date: Date; fruit: string; value: number }[]; columns: Date[]; }
charts.when_to_use: A multi-series line chart where labels sit on the lines at each column, so no legend lookup is needed.

charts.title: Directly Labelling Lines
charts.data_shape: { name: string; values: { year: number; value: number }[] }[]
charts.when_to_use: A multi-series line chart where each line is named at its own right end, so the eye never round-trips to a legend.

charts.title: Icicle
charts.data_shape: { name: string; value?: number; children?: Data[] }
charts.when_to_use: Shows a hierarchy's depth and each node's share as nested rows, when a treemap's shuffled rectangles would hide the level structure.

charts.title: Dendrogram
charts.data_shape: { name: string; children?: Data[] }
charts.when_to_use: A taxonomy where every leaf matters equally, so all leaves align on one edge instead of being spaced by depth like a tidy tree.

charts.title: Indented Tree
charts.data_shape: { name: string; value?: number; children?: Data[] }
charts.when_to_use: A hierarchy read as a list of indented rows with per-node counts and sizes, for trees far deeper than they are wide.

charts.title: Hierarchical Bar Chart
charts.data_shape: { tree: RegionNode; focus: string[] }
charts.when_to_use: Ranks the children of one node in a value hierarchy as bars on a shared scale, for reading a breakdown one level at a time.

charts.title: Nested Treemap
charts.data_shape: { name: string; value?: number; children?: Data[] }
charts.when_to_use: Sizes leaves by value while keeping every intermediate group visible as a labelled frame, unlike a flat treemap that shows only leaves.

charts.title: Cascaded Treemap
charts.data_shape: { name: string; value?: number; children?: Data[] }
charts.when_to_use: A nested treemap where each level overhangs its parent with a drop shadow, so several levels of nesting stay readable.

charts.title: Sequences Sunburst
charts.data_shape: { sequences: { path: string; count: number }[]; steps: string[]; }
charts.when_to_use: Traces the ordered paths people take through a funnel, each ring a further step, with a breadcrumb naming the hovered route.

charts.title: Tree of Life

charts.title: Bubble Chart

keywords: flat list of name and value

charts.title: Smallest Enclosing Circle
charts.data_shape: number[]
charts.when_to_use: Packs a bare list of radii into tangent circles and draws the smallest circle containing them all, with no hierarchy involved.

charts.title: Stern-Brocot Tree
charts.when_to_use: Lays out a binary tree whose nodes are generated by a rule rather than supplied as data, here every positive rational as a fraction.

charts.title: Chord Diagram
charts.data_shape: { names: string[]; matrix: number[][] }
charts.when_to_use: Two-way flows among a small set of groups, where each pair's exchange in both directions has to be read at once.

charts.title: Directed Chord Diagram
charts.data_shape: { source: string; target: string; value: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Flows among groups where direction matters and each ribbon's two ends differ, built from a source-target-value edge list rather than a matrix.

charts.title: Chord Dependency Diagram
charts.data_shape: { source: string; target: string; value: number }[]
charts.when_to_use: Directed dependencies among many named modules laid out as a ring, when a force graph of the same edges would be a hairball.

charts.title: Hierarchical Edge Bundling
charts.data_shape: { tree: ModuleNode; groups: string[] }
charts.when_to_use: Relations between the leaves of a hierarchy, routed through common ancestors so hundreds of edges read as bundles instead of a mesh.

charts.title: Bilevel Edge Bundling
charts.data_shape: { name: string; children?: Data[]; imports?: string[] }
charts.when_to_use: Hierarchical edge bundling coloured by whether each node mostly imports or is mostly imported, when the direction of coupling is the question.

charts.title: Labelled Chord Diagram
charts.data_shape: { names: string[]; matrix: number[][] }
charts.when_to_use: A chord diagram carrying a graduated ruler around the ring, for when readers need absolute magnitudes and not just relative arc size.

charts.title: Force-Directed Graph

charts.title: Disjoint Force-Directed Graph

charts.title: Force-Directed Tree

charts.when_to_use: A hierarchy laid out by simulation instead of a tidy tree, when you want organic branching and no fixed depth columns.

charts.title: Mobile Patent Suits
charts.data_shape: { companies: string[]; suits: { source: string; target: string; type: SuitType }[]; types: SuitType[]; }
charts.when_to_use: A directed network where edge type and reciprocity matter: every link bows so mutual edges do not overdraw, and arrowheads carry direction.

charts.title: Temporal Force-Directed Graph
charts.data_shape: { nodes: { id: string; group: string; start: number; end: number }[]; links: { source: string; target: string; start: number; end: number }[]; frames: number[]; topics: string[]; }

charts.title: Tangled Tree

charts.title: Parallel Sets
charts.data_shape: { rows: Outcome[]; dimensions: { key: Exclude<keyof Outcome, 'count'>; label: string }[]; }
charts.when_to_use: Follows how records split across several categorical stages, for columns that are categories rather than the numbers parallel coordinates needs.

charts.title: Scatterplot Matrix
charts.data_shape: { rows: Penguin[]; dimensions: { key: PenguinDimension; label: string }[]; species: string[]; }
charts.when_to_use: Every pair of numeric columns plotted at once, to find which pair actually correlates before committing to a single scatterplot.

charts.title: Brushable Scatterplot Matrix
charts.data_shape: { rows: Penguin[]; dimensions: { key: PenguinDimension; label: string }[]; species: PenguinSpecies[]; }

charts.title: Radial Stacked Bar Chart

charts.title: Radial Area Chart

charts.title: Radial Dendrogram
charts.data_shape: { name: string; children?: Data[] }

charts.title: Radial Tidy Tree

charts.title: World Map

charts.title: World Choropleth
charts.data_shape: Map<string, number>

charts.title: US State Choropleth

charts.title: Bivariate Choropleth

charts.title: Bubble Map

charts.title: Spike Map

charts.title: Projection Comparison

charts.title: Tissot's Indicatrix

charts.title: US Airports Voronoi

charts.title: Hexbin Map
charts.data_shape: { lon: number; lat: number; year: number }[]

charts.title: Solar Terminator

charts.title: Star Map

charts.title: Spilhaus Shoreline Map

charts.title: Walmart's Growth

charts.when_to_use: Animates dated point locations appearing over time to show how a network spread geographically, not just where it ended up.

charts.title: Antimeridian Cutting
charts.when_to_use: Demonstrates how a continuously rotated projection cuts geometry at the antimeridian instead of streaking it across the frame.

charts.title: Graticule Labels (Stereographic)
charts.when_to_use: Annotates meridians and parallels with their coordinates around a hemisphere's rim, when readers need to locate positions rather than just see shapes.

charts.title: Orthographic to Equirectangular
charts.when_to_use: Morphs a globe into a flat map by interpolating the raw projections, showing that the two are the same surface unrolled.

charts.title: Projection Transitions
charts.when_to_use: Cycles smoothly through a dozen world projections so their differences show up as motion rather than as a static grid.

charts.title: Versor Dragging
charts.when_to_use: Lets a reader drag a globe to any orientation with the grabbed point staying under the cursor, for exploring geography interactively.

charts.title: World Tour
charts.data_shape: string[]

charts.title: World Airports Voronoi

charts.title: Word Cloud
charts.data_shape: { text: string; count: number }[]

charts.title: Label Occlusion

charts.title: Quicksort

charts.title: Maze by Random Traversal
charts.when_to_use: Showing the plainest spanning-tree maze generator, taking a uniformly random edge off the frontier, as a baseline for the other three.

charts.title: Maze by Randomized Depth-First
charts.when_to_use: Showing why depth-first carving produces long winding corridors and deep dead ends, unlike the frontier-based generators.

charts.title: Maze by Randomized Prim's
charts.when_to_use: Showing Prim's growing outward from a single seed by lowest-weight frontier edge, giving a bushy maze with short dead ends.

charts.title: Maze by Wilson's Algorithm
charts.when_to_use: Showing Wilson's loop-erased random walk, the one generator that samples spanning trees uniformly and so has no structural bias.

charts.title: Maze Flood Fill
charts.when_to_use: Colouring a graph by distance from an origin, when the reader should see the wavefront sweep outward rather than a static heat map.

charts.title: Maze as Tidy Tree
charts.when_to_use: Re-encoding the same structure two ways to prove a claim, here that a maze is literally a spanning tree once you straighten it out.

charts.title: Fisher-Yates Shuffle
charts.when_to_use: Teaching the Fisher-Yates invariant, that everything from i rightwards is already final, by shading that region as it grows.

charts.title: Shuffle Bias Matrix
charts.when_to_use: Proving an algorithm is biased empirically: two heatmaps of where each element lands over many trials, on one shared colour scale.

charts.title: Quadtree Subdivision
charts.when_to_use: Showing why a spatial index is fast: which cells a nearest-neighbour search actually visited and which whole subtrees it threw away.

charts.title: Maze by Kruskal's Algorithm
charts.when_to_use: Showing Kruskal's committing the cheapest edges in global order, so scattered fragments appear everywhere at once and fuse into one spanning tree — the contrast to Prim's single growing blob.

charts.title: Pathfinding Compared
charts.when_to_use: Racing breadth-first, Dijkstra, greedy best-first and A* on one shared weighted terrain, when the reader should see each frontier's shape — the wave, the blinkered tongue, the ellipse — and the cells-expanded scoreboard.

charts.title: String Search: Naive vs Boyer-Moore
charts.when_to_use: Racing naive and Boyer-Moore over the same text one comparison per tick, when the point is what is never read — letters gray out as they are examined and Boyer-Moore's ribbon stays mostly bright.

charts.title: Wave Function Collapse
charts.when_to_use: Showing constraint propagation assembling a pipe circuit: the least-certain cell collapses, constraints ripple outward, and an entropy heat map drains until the grid is decided.

charts.title: Bloom Filter
charts.when_to_use: Showing a Bloom filter earning its space savings: inserts light three hashed bits in a 256-bit grid, true negatives bounce off a dark bit, and the reader witnesses the first false positive — a word never inserted whose bits were all set by others.

charts.title: Radix Sort
charts.when_to_use: Showing order emerging from classification instead of comparison: 24 three-digit base-4 values drawn as stacked digit-color bands settle digit by digit, positions tweening as each pass groups by one digit and the comparison counter stays at zero.

charts.title: Edit Distance Wavefront
charts.when_to_use: Showing dynamic programming as a wavefront: the INTENTION-to-EXECUTION edit distance matrix fills along anti-diagonals, then the traceback lights backwards from the corner and the optimal alignment materializes above it.

charts.title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
charts.when_to_use: Showing the Sieve of Eratosthenes striking composites in layered translucent colors, one sweep per prime up to √300, so primes are what is left blank — and the reader sees why stopping at the square root is legal.

charts.title: Lloyd Relaxation
charts.when_to_use: Showing iterative convergence decelerating: every Voronoi site jumps to its cell centroid, and the displacement whiskers shrink from early leaps to late trembles as the tessellation settles, with max movement captioned per iteration.

charts.title: k-Means Clustering
charts.when_to_use: Showing k-means alternate its assign and update phases on gaussian blobs: boundary points flicker between cluster colors for several rounds before equilibrium, with the count of switched points captioned each round.

charts.title: Gradient Descent Compared
charts.when_to_use: Racing SGD, momentum and Adam down one two-basin loss surface when the reader should see optimizer temperament: SGD zigzags under noise, momentum overshoots the valley and swings back, Adam hugs the slope, each captioned with its current loss.

charts.title: Union-Find Path Compression
charts.when_to_use: Making amortized analysis physical: naive unions chain a forest into tall trees, then one path-compressing find drags every walked node directly under the root and the tree height visibly collapses, with depth before and after captioned.

charts.title: Huffman Coding
charts.when_to_use: Showing greed on the two lightest trees building the provably optimal prefix code: the forest merges bottom-up, then the sentence encodes live with the variable-length bit count racing fixed-width.

charts.title: Reservoir Sampling
charts.when_to_use: Showing a stream flowing past a fixed-size reservoir where each later arrival is kept with shrinking probability k/i, yet every element ends equally likely — the fading arrival opacity is the odds.

charts.title: Skip List
charts.when_to_use: Showing randomized towers buying binary-search speed in a linked list: one search descends level by level and the dim never-visited majority is the payoff — the skipping-work encoding applied to a structure.

charts.title: Consistent Hashing
charts.when_to_use: Showing keys and nodes on a hash ring through scripted joins and leaves: the moved keys flash and arc to their new owner while the unmoved majority stays put, and the moved-versus-total counter is the argument.
